title: Verifier-Guided Evaluation of LLM-Generated Network Configurations: a Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study that measured whether a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (generate→validate→repair, ≤1 repair) improves correctness of LLM-generated network configurations relative to single-shot initial generation. Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and an automated network verifier, we ran 200 preregistered intent→configuration tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused for both baseline and guarded episodes). The hosted model was gpt-5-mini (model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset). Baseline configurations passed all verifier-specified invariants in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline passed 200/200 tasks (100%). The paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.015]); discordant pairs n10=1, n01=0; exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0. The single guarded improvement resulted from one verifier-triggered repair invocation that corrected a multi-step ordering failure. We report the preregistration, execution artifacts, complete paired analysis, a short failure-mode diagnosis, and limitations (synthetic tasks, single model, shared_initial_candidate semantics).

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate high-level operator intent into low-level device configurations for network operations (NetOps). Operational adoption requires that generated artifacts satisfy deterministic invariants such as reachability, policy compliance, loop‑freedom, and ordered-change/workflow constraints. Prior work has proposed prototype intent→configuration systems and benchmark-style evaluations (prototype intent→config pipelines [1]) and separately developed formal/verifier-driven approaches for policy and reachability checking (deterministic verifier approaches [2]). Cross-domain literature advocates pairing generation with external validators or repair loops to mitigate unsafe outputs (generate→validate→repair demonstrated in program-repair and test-in-the-loop contexts [4]). Reporting guidelines for LLM studies emphasize preregistration and artifact disclosure to improve reproducibility [3]. This study asks: under shared_initial_candidate semantics (the same initial generation reused for baseline and guarded episodes), to what extent does a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (one permitted repair call) reduce invariant violations relative to single-shot initial generation? We answer this with a preregistered paired evaluation (N=200 tasks) executed with a deterministic synthetic task generator, a deterministic network verifier, and a hosted LLM (gpt-5-mini), with all artifacts archived.
sections.related_work: Work on LLM-driven NetOps includes intent→configuration prototypes and benchmarks that explore whether models can synthesize device configurations from natural-language intent (e.g., NetConfEval-style evaluations; prototype intent→config pipelines [1]). Network-verification research has produced deterministic or formal validators that serve as oracles for reachability and policy compliance (formal/verifier-driven methods applied to configuration verification [2]). Cross-domain evidence shows that generator+validator+repair architectures materially improve verifiability in program repair and related engineering tasks (generate→validate→repair in program/decompilation/code-repair contexts [4], tool-augmented LLM agents for analysis [6]). Surveys and safety analyses highlight hallucination and failure modes and recommend guardrails, provenance, and verifier stages for operational pipelines (LLM-survey and evaluation guidance [5]; LLM reporting guidelines [3]). The present experiment situates a tightly controlled, verifier-centered empirical test within these strands by providing an artifact-backed paired assessment of verifier-triggered repairs under shared_initial_candidate semantics.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand: We preregistered study CAND-2026-001 before outcome observation. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline — per-task binary indicator that the deterministic verifier accepts the generated configuration (all specified invariants pass). Sampling and tasks: 200 deterministic intent→configuration tasks were produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 targeting very_hard and extreme workflow patterns. Design and generation semantics: the preregistered design fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate: exactly one initial generation was sampled per task and deterministically reused for both baseline and guarded episodes; independent first-pass generations for each condition were not produced (this design makes the estimand measure only the effect of the verifier/repair stage). Model and execution: the hosted adapter was hosted_netops_gvr_v1 calling the declared model gpt-5-mini; the model_configuration recorded temperature = null/unset — null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. The adapter permitted at most one automated repair call per task; the execution manifest records hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; repair = 1), consistent with the shared_initial_candidate contract. Validation and scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 performed full intent-constraint validation (syntactic parsing, per-device allowed-field checks, encoded workflow/ordering policies, and network-level invariants). Per-task outcome is binary: 'all invariants pass' vs 'any invariant fails'. Analysis plan: primary confirmatory test used an exact McNemar-style paired test with discordant-pair reporting; per-condition pass rates reported with 95% Wilson CIs; paired bootstrap percentile CI for the risk difference used 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). All prompts, model-call traces, verifier logs, task manifests, and analysis artifacts were archived and are referenced in the execution manifest.
sections.results: Execution and accounting: The run completed as preregistered (planned episodes = 400; completed episodes = 400). Provider accounting: hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 (200 shared initial-generation calls + 1 repair call). Primary confirmatory outcomes: baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded successes = 200/200 (1.0). Paired contingency table: n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (rows: guarded; columns: baseline). Paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the difference = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Repair activity: the guarded pipeline invoked its single permitted repair once; that repair converted the lone baseline failure into a guarded success. Failure diagnosis: the repaired task's validator trace (archived) indicates a multi-step ordering constraint spanning interfaces (a workflow ordering violation) that required a corrected sequence of operations; the repair prompt produced the corrected ordering and the verifier accepted the repaired candidate. Missingness/exclusions: there were no preregistered exclusions, no unparsable persistent outputs, and no failed episodes under the preregistered handling rules.
sections.discussion: Scientific interpretation: Under the chosen synthetic corpus, verifier encoding of operational invariants, and gpt-5-mini generation, single-shot LLM outputs already satisfied verifier-specified invariants in 199/200 tasks; the guarded pipeline's single repair corrected the single remaining multi-step ordering failure. Because generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, the paired outcome difference arises solely from verifier-triggered repair rather than independent first-pass generation differences. Statistical and power perspective: the preregistration targeted detection of a 10–15 percentage-point absolute change assuming baseline rates ~45–65%; the observed baseline (~99.5%) was far higher, rendering the original power assumptions inapplicable. The paired bootstrap 95% CI upper bound (0.015) quantifies the realized detectable absolute improvement range given this run. Practical implications are therefore narrowly bounded: deterministic verifier gates with a bounded repair can remediate specific multi-step ordering faults in this synthetic corpus, but broader operational claims require multi-model, larger/diverse tasks, independent first-pass comparisons, or live-device evaluation. Threats to validity: internal validity is limited by shared_initial_candidate semantics (no independent first-pass contrast), potential oracle (validator) incompleteness, and a single-model evaluation. Construct validity: the verifier enforces encoded invariants but does not observe runtime device behaviors only visible via live execution. External validity: tasks are synthetic and topologies controlled; no adversarial contamination experiments were executed. Relation to prior work: this experiment operationalizes a generator→validator→repair design advocated in prior engineering domains (generate→validate→repair shown in program repair/test-in-the-loop [4]) and connects to intent→config prototype evaluations in NetOps research (prototype intent→config pipelines [1]) while explicitly providing archived, deterministic verifier-backed artifacts for reproducibility.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired evaluation of a verifier-guarded intent→configuration pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics. In this deterministic synthetic task corpus with gpt-5-mini, single-shot generation yielded very high verifier compliance (199/200), and a single verifier-triggered repair converted the sole failing case into success, producing a small absolute improvement (0.5 percentage points). The archival bundle documents the end-to-end generator→validator→repair pipeline, execution accounting (hosted_model_call_event_count = 201; shared_initial_generation = 200; repair = 1), and analysis artifacts to support reproducibility. Future work should evaluate multiple models, larger and more diverse task banks including noisy or partial state and live-device semantics, independent first-pass comparisons (when the estimand requires them), adversarial contamination, and richer runtime oracles.

limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and the deterministic verifier; they do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent prompt-engineering or constrained-generation effects.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.
